rows.where: Design § Architecture 5 — deploy-freshness.yml on cron '0 15 * * *', fetch-depth: 0, describe-services → services[0].taskDefinition → describe-task-definition on that revision ARN → tag → git log -1 --format=%ct, fail when the gap exceeds 7 days; § Resolved question 1
rows.note: Upgraded from partial: the fidelity gap is resolved and the reasoning checks out. services[0].taskDefinition is the revision ARN the service is actually on, and the design's justification for why deploy-services' family-name lookup is right there but wrong here is correct — deploy-services declares `needs: [run-migrator, terraform-prod, deploy-images, detect-changes]` gated on `needs.terraform-prod.result == 'success'`, so it genuinely runs after terraform-prod wrote the revision. Residual shared-fate with GitHub Actions is an argued, accepted trade-off, and the design correctly rejects the in-ci.yml option for the exact reason it would have failed in this incident.
